None of this says the brain is equipotential. Regions differ in their connections and 
contributions, and the asymmetries catalogued in Section 3 depend on those differences. 
But a structure may set the terms for other processes while having its own terms set in turn: 
it is controller or controlled depending on the process. The same is true in any densely 
cross-linked network, where a junction is upstream of one route and downstream of 
another. Thus “above” and “below” are directions of travel, not fixed addresses. This alone 
is insufficient for heterarchy: the relations must be relations of control and must fail to 
compose within the behavioral capacity and occasions being explained.
